name: Spanish 21
description: Spanish 21 (known internationally as Pontoon in Australia, not UK classic Pontoon) is a variant of Blackjack played with 'Spanish' decks (48 cards, removing the 10s). The removal of 10s increases the house edge, but this is compensated by extremely player-friendly rules such as 'Player 21 always wins', 'Surrender after Double', and special bonus payouts for specific 21 combinations (6-7-8, 7-7-7). It is highly popular in casinos.
deck: Spanish Deck (48 cards: Remove 10s from Standard 52. J, Q, K are still 10 value). Often 6-8 decks.

history.origins: Introduced in Nevada casinos in 1995 by Masque Publishing. Based on the lack of 10s which favors the house.
timeline: Present: Known for having a comparable house edge to Blackjack if played optimally.
history.cultural: Attracts players who enjoy the bonus payouts and the 'fun' rules like Late Surrender.
history.evolution: Australian Pontoon is essentially Spanish 21 with different terminology ('Pontoon' for Blackjack, 'Stick' for Stand).

setup.players: One to seven players at the table, each playing independently against the dealer. Standard blackjack layout; six or eight Spanish decks in a shoe.
setup.dealing: Standard Blackjack deal. 2 cards each. Dealer gets hole card.

rules.objective: Beat the dealer's hand total without going over 21. A hand total of 21 is best; player 21 always wins, including against dealer blackjack.
rules.gameplay: Players place a bet. Dealer gives two cards to each player and two to himself (one dealer card face-up). Players act in turn: hit (draw), stand (pass), double down, split pairs, or surrender. Player 21 always wins. Player blackjack beats dealer blackjack. Late surrender and double-after-split are allowed. Dealer then plays according to house rules (hit or stand on soft 17). Hands are compared; higher total without busting wins. Bonuses pay for 6-7-8, 7-7-7, and multi-card 21.
keyRules: Spanish deck: 48 cards (no 10s); face cards count 10.
Late surrender allowed. Double after split and re-split aces allowed.
Player may double on any number of cards. Hit and double after splitting aces (where offered).
Surrender after doubling (double down rescue) forfeits original bet.
Five-card 21 pays 3:2; six-card 21 pays 2:1; seven-plus-card 21 pays 3:1.
6-7-8 or 7-7-7 mixed suits 3:2; same suit 2:1; spades 3:1. Suited 7-7-7 vs dealer 7 pays Super Bonus.

strategy.basic: Do not use standard Blackjack strategy! The missing 10s change the math significantly. You hit more often on stiff hands (12-16) because the bust card (10) is gone. You double less often against dealer's 2-6 because dealer is less likely to bust.
strategy.intermediate: Surrender: Use the 'Double Rescue' option freely if your double goes bad (e.g., Doubling 11, getting a 2 for 13 against a dealer Ace? Surrender).
strategy.advanced: Bonus Hunting: Sometimes hitting a hard 14 (composed of 7-7) against a dealer 6 is correct to fish for the third 7.

variations.name: Dealer stands on soft 17
variations.description: House rule: dealer stands on soft 17. Lower house edge (about 0.40%).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dealer soft-17 rule is a house constant; engine overrides for it can be added when supported.

variations.name: Dealer hits soft 17
variations.description: House rule: dealer hits soft 17. Redoubling allowed (up to three times) gives house edge about 0.42%; without redoubling about 0.76%.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Dealer soft-17 and redouble rules are house options; engine overrides can be added when supported.

scoring.description: Beat dealer's total without busting. 21 is best.
scoring.winCondition: Beat dealer's total without busting. 21 is best.
